**Mario Gabriele Andretti** (born February 28, 1940) is an American former [racing driver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Racing_driver "Racing driver") who competed in [Formula One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Formula_One "Formula One") from [1968](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1968_Formula_One_season "1968 Formula One season") to [1982](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1982_Formula_One_World_Championship "1982 Formula One World Championship"), and [IndyCar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_open-wheel_racing "American open-wheel racing") from [1964](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1964_USAC_Championship_Car_season "1964 USAC Championship Car season") to [1994](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1994_IndyCar_season "1994 IndyCar season"). Andretti won the [Formula One World Drivers' Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Formula_One_World_Drivers'_Championship "Formula One World Drivers' Championship") in [1978](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1978_Formula_One_season "1978 Formula One season") with [Lotus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Lotus "Team Lotus"), and won 12 [Grands Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Formula_One_Grands_Prix "Formula One Grands Prix") across 14 seasons. In [American open-wheel racing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_open-wheel_racing "American open-wheel racing"), Andretti won four [IndyCar National Championship titles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_American_open-wheel_racing_national_champions "List of American open-wheel racing national champions") and the [Indianapolis 500](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indianapolis_500 "Indianapolis 500") in [1969](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1969_Indianapolis_500 "1969 Indianapolis 500"); in [stock car racing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stock_car_racing "Stock car racing"), he won the [Daytona 500](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daytona_500 "Daytona 500") in [1967](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1967_Daytona_500 "1967 Daytona 500"). In [endurance racing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Endurance_racing_(motorsport) "Endurance racing (motorsport)"), Andretti is a three-time winner of the [12 Hours of Sebring](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/12_Hours_of_Sebring "12 Hours of Sebring").

Andretti and his family were displaced from Italian-controlled [Istria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Istria "Istria") during the [Istrian–Dalmatian exodus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Istrian%E2%80%93Dalmatian_exodus "Istrian–Dalmatian exodus") and eventually emigrated to [Nazareth, Pennsylvania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nazareth,_Pennsylvania "Nazareth, Pennsylvania") in 1955. He began [dirt track racing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dirt_track_racing "Dirt track racing") with his twin brother [Aldo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aldo_Andretti "Aldo Andretti") four years later, with Andretti progressing to [USAC Championship Car](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USAC_Championship_Car "USAC Championship Car") in [1964](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1964_USAC_Championship_Car_season "1964 USAC Championship Car season"). In [open-wheel racing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_open-wheel_racing "American open-wheel racing"), he won back-to-back [USAC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Auto_Club "United States Auto Club") titles in [1965](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1965_USAC_Championship_Car_season "1965 USAC Championship Car season") and [1966](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1966_USAC_Championship_Car_season "1966 USAC Championship Car season"), also finishing runner-up in [1967](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1967_USAC_Championship_Car_season "1967 USAC Championship Car season") and [1968](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1968_USAC_Championship_Car_season "1968 USAC Championship Car season"). He also contested [stock car racing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stock_car_racing "Stock car racing") in his early career, winning the [1967 Daytona 500](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1967_Daytona_500 "1967 Daytona 500") with [Holman-Moody](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holman-Moody "Holman-Moody"). He took his first major [sportscar racing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sportscar_racing "Sportscar racing") victory at the [12 Hours of Sebring](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1967_12_Hours_of_Sebring "1967 12 Hours of Sebring") that year with [Ford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ford_Motor_Company "Ford Motor Company"). Andretti debuted in Formula One at the [United States Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1968_United_States_Grand_Prix "1968 United States Grand Prix") in [1968](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1968_Formula_One_season "1968 Formula One season") with [Lotus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Lotus "Team Lotus"), where he qualified on [pole position](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Formula_One_polesitters "List of Formula One polesitters"). He contested several further Grands Prix with Lotus in [1969](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1969_Formula_One_season "1969 Formula One season"), when he won his [third USAC title](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1969_USAC_Championship_Car_season "1969 USAC Championship Car season") and the [Indianapolis 500](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1969_Indianapolis_500 "1969 Indianapolis 500"). In [1970](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1970_Formula_One_season "1970 Formula One season"), Andretti took his maiden podium finish at the [Spanish Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1970_Spanish_Grand_Prix "1970 Spanish Grand Prix") with [STP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STP_(motor_oil_company) "STP (motor oil company)"), driving a [privateer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Privateer_(motorsport) "Privateer (motorsport)")[March 701](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/March_701 "March 701"). He signed for [Ferrari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scuderia_Ferrari "Scuderia Ferrari") that year, winning [at Sebring](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1970_12_Hours_of_Sebring "1970 12 Hours of Sebring") again.

Andretti took his maiden victory in Formula One at the season-opening [South African Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1971_South_African_Grand_Prix "1971 South African Grand Prix") in [1971](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1971_Formula_One_season "1971 Formula One season"), on debut for Ferrari. He took his third Sebring victory the [following year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1972_12_Hours_of_Sebring "1972 12 Hours of Sebring"). After part-time roles for Ferrari and [Parnelli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parnelli "Parnelli") in [1972](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1972_Formula_One_season "1972 Formula One season") and [1974](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1974_Formula_One_season "1974 Formula One season"), respectively, Andretti joined the latter full-time for [1975](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1975_Formula_One_season "1975 Formula One season") after finishing runner-up in the [SCCA Continental Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1974_SCCA/USAC_Formula_5000_Championship "1974 SCCA/USAC Formula 5000 Championship"). He moved back to Lotus in [1976](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1976_Formula_One_season "1976 Formula One season"), winning the season-ending [Japanese Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1976_Japanese_Grand_Prix "1976 Japanese Grand Prix") and helping develop the [78](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lotus_78 "Lotus 78"). Andretti won four Grands Prix in [1977](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1977_Formula_One_season "1977 Formula One season"), finishing third in the [World Drivers' Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Drivers'_Championship "World Drivers' Championship"). He won the title in [1978](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1978_Formula_One_season "1978 Formula One season") after achieving six victories, becoming the [second World Drivers' Champion from the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Formula_One_drivers_from_the_United_States "Formula One drivers from the United States"). After winless [1979](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1979_Formula_One_season "1979 Formula One season") and [1980](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1980_Formula_One_season "1980 Formula One season") campaigns with Lotus, he moved to [Alfa Romeo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfa_Romeo_in_Formula_One "Alfa Romeo in Formula One") in [1981](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1981_Formula_One_World_Championship "1981 Formula One World Championship"). Following two fill-in appearances for [Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Williams_Racing "Williams Racing") and Ferrari in [1982](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1982_Formula_One_World_Championship "1982 Formula One World Championship"), Andretti retired from Formula One with 12 wins, 18 pole positions, 10 fastest laps and 19 podiums.

Andretti returned to full-time IndyCar racing in [1982](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1982_CART_PPG_Indy_Car_World_Series "1982 CART PPG Indy Car World Series"), placing third in the standings with [Patrick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patrick_Racing "Patrick Racing"), amongst winning the [Michigan 500](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1982_Michigan_500 "1982 Michigan 500"). After finishing third again with [Newman/Haas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newman/Haas_Racing "Newman/Haas Racing") in his [1983](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1983_CART_PPG_Indy_Car_World_Series "1983 CART PPG Indy Car World Series") campaign, he won his fourth IndyCar title in [1984](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1984_CART_PPG_Indy_Car_World_Series "1984 CART PPG Indy Car World Series"), 15 years after the previous and his first sanctioned by [CART](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Championship_Auto_Racing_Teams "Championship Auto Racing Teams"). He won the [Pocono 500](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_Pocono_500 "1986 Pocono 500") in [1986](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_CART_PPG_Indy_Car_World_Series "1986 CART PPG Indy Car World Series") and remained with Newman/Haas until [1994](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1994_CART_PPG_Indy_Car_World_Series "1994 CART PPG Indy Car World Series"); his victory at [Phoenix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Bryan_Memorial "Jimmy Bryan Memorial") in [1993](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1993_CART_PPG_Indy_Car_World_Series "1993 CART PPG Indy Car World Series") made him the oldest winner in IndyCar history, aged 53, as well as the first driver to win a race in four different decades. Andretti retired with 52 wins, 65 pole positions, and 141 podiums in IndyCar. His 111 official victories on major circuits across several motorsport disciplines saw his name become synonymous with speed in American popular culture.[[b]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-3) His sons, [Michael](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Andretti "Michael Andretti") and [Jeff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeff_Andretti "Jeff Andretti"), were both racing drivers, the former winning the CART title in [1991](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1991_CART_PPG_Indy_Car_World_Series "1991 CART PPG Indy Car World Series") and previously owning [Andretti Global](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andretti_Global "Andretti Global"). Andretti serves on the board of directors of [Cadillac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cadillac_in_Formula_One "Cadillac in Formula One") in Formula One from its debut in [2026](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Formula_One_World_Championship "2026 Formula One World Championship") onwards. He was inducted into the [International Motorsports Hall of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Motorsports_Hall_of_Fame "International Motorsports Hall of Fame") in 2000.

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mario_Andretti&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

### Childhood in Italy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mario_Andretti&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Childhood in Italy")]

Mario Gabriele Andretti was born on February 28, 1940,[[c]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-6) to an [Istrian-Italian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Istrian_Italians "Istrian Italians") family in [Montona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Montona_d'Istria "Montona d'Istria"), Istria, Kingdom of Italy (present-day Motovun, Croatia).[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Personal_life-7)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-sportscentury-8) He was born six hours before his twin brother [Aldo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aldo_Andretti "Aldo Andretti").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Comiskey%E2%80%932017-9) He is the son of Alvise "Gigi" Andretti, who worked as a farm administrator in Italy and for [Bethlehem Steel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bethlehem_Steel "Bethlehem Steel") in the U.S.,[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-10)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Reinhard%E2%80%932016-11) and his wife Rina.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-12) He also had an older sister, Anna Maria Andretti Burley.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-13)

Andretti's family owned a 2,100-acre (850 ha) farm in Montona,[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Andretti%E2%80%932016-14) but after World War II, the [Treaty of Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris_Peace_Treaties,_1947 "Paris Peace Treaties, 1947") (1947) transferred the territory to [communist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Communist_Party_of_Yugoslavia "Communist Party of Yugoslavia")-controlled [Yugoslavia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yugoslavia "Yugoslavia"). As a result, the Andretti family joined the [Istrian–Dalmatian exodus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Istrian%E2%80%93Dalmatian_exodus "Istrian–Dalmatian exodus") in 1948. The family lost all their land and was permitted to take only one truckload of possessions.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Andretti%E2%80%932016-14) They spent seven years in a refugee camp in [Lucca](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lucca "Lucca"),[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Lawrence%E2%80%932015-15) living in an abandoned college dormitory without running water.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Reinhard%E2%80%932016-11)

The Andretti twins were interested in racing at an early age. At age five, they raced hand-crafted wooden cars through the Montona streets.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-milwaukee-16) After moving to Lucca, the brothers got a job parking cars at a local garage.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Gushue%E2%80%932016-17) In his autobiography, Andretti wrote, "The first time I fired up a car, felt the engine shudder and the wheel come to life in my hands, I was hooked. It was a feeling I can't describe. I still get it every time I get into a race car."[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Bantam%E2%80%931970-18):6

The garage owners noticed the brothers' passion for racing and brought them to watch the [1954 Mille Miglia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1954_Mille_Miglia "1954 Mille Miglia"), which was won by two-time Formula One champion [Alberto Ascari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alberto_Ascari "Alberto Ascari").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Gushue%E2%80%932016-17)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-mshf-19) Ascari became Andretti's personal idol.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-20)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Andretti%E2%80%932015-21) The twins also visited [Monza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autodromo_Nazionale_Monza "Autodromo Nazionale Monza") for the [Italian Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1954_Italian_Grand_Prix "1954 Italian Grand Prix"), where Andretti saw Ascari race against [Juan Manuel Fangio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juan_Manuel_Fangio "Juan Manuel Fangio").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Andretti%E2%80%932015-21) Although the twins did not have a grandstand seat, Andretti recalled "being just mesmerized, overwhelmed by the sound, by the speed."[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Gushue%E2%80%932016-17)

### Move to the United States

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mario_Andretti&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Move to the United States")]

Following a three-year wait for U.S. visas, the Andretti family moved to the United States in 1955. After an eleven-day journey on the [SS _Conte Biancamano_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SS_Conte_Biancamano "SS Conte Biancamano"), they sailed into [New York Harbor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Harbor "New York Harbor") on Anna Maria's birthday of June 16.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Comiskey%E2%80%932017-9)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-22) With just $125 in cash, they settled in [Nazareth, Pennsylvania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nazareth,_Pennsylvania "Nazareth, Pennsylvania"), where Alvise Andretti's brother-in-law Tony lived. Although Alvise planned to leave after five years, the family never left the United States.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Andretti%E2%80%932016-14)

Andretti opposed leaving Italy at the time.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Andretti%E2%80%932016-14) His father felt that moving to America would give his children the best opportunity to succeed in life,[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-auto-23) but did not want his sons to become motor racers, as the sport was extremely dangerous at the time.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Andretti%E2%80%932016-14) Andretti planned to become a welder,[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-ESPNclassic-24) but racing was "the only passion [he] really had career wise," and he admitted that he might not have been able to become a racer if he had stayed in Italy.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-auto-23) Andretti's father did not watch him race until Andretti reached IndyCar in 1964.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-25)

In his 1970 biography, Andretti said that he became a [naturalized](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naturalization "Naturalization") U.S. citizen on April 15, 1964.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Bantam%E2%80%931970-18):xiii (His IndyCar debut was April 19, 1964).[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-ESPN-26) Andretti later revealed that he actually obtained U.S. citizenship on April 7, 1965.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Naturalization-5)

## Early racing career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mario_Andretti&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Early racing career")]

### Debut in dirt track racing

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mario_Andretti&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Debut in dirt track racing")]

[![Image 7](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/84/Mario_and_aldo.jpg/250px-Mario_and_aldo.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Mario_and_aldo.jpg)

Mario (left) and his brother [Aldo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aldo_Andretti "Aldo Andretti") at the [2007 Indianapolis 500](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Indianapolis_500 "2007 Indianapolis 500") pole day

The first car Andretti regularly drove was his father's 1957 Chevrolet, which the twins did not race, but nonetheless upgraded with features like a [glasspack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glasspack "Glasspack") muffler and fuel injection.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Gushue%E2%80%932016-17) The twins were surprised to find that Nazareth hosted a half-mile [dirt track](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dirt_track_racing "Dirt track racing"), [Nazareth Speedway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nazareth_Speedway "Nazareth Speedway").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-sportscentury-8) They used money they made working at their uncle's [Sunoco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunoco "Sunoco") station[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Andretti%E2%80%932016-14) to refurbish a 1948 [Hudson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hudson_Super_Six "Hudson Super Six"),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-sportscentury-8) using a stolen beer barrel as a fuel tank.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Andretti%E2%80%932016-14) The car was ready to race when the twins were 19 years old, but the minimum age to race was 21, so the brothers convinced a newspaper editor to falsify their drivers' licenses.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Andretti%E2%80%932016-14) After Aldo got into a major accident, the local chief of police spotted the forgery but turned a blind eye to save Aldo's health insurance.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Gushue%E2%80%932016-17)

The twins did not tell their father that they were racing until Aldo fractured his skull in a race and spent 62 days in a coma. Andretti's father nearly disowned Mario when the latter insisted on racing again, but eventually relented. Aldo also resumed racing, but suffered a career-ending accident in 1969.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Andretti%E2%80%932016-14)

The twins got off to a good start, picking up two wins each in [sportsman racing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASCAR_Sportsman_Division "NASCAR Sportsman Division") after their first four races.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-ESPN-26) In their first two weeks of racing, they won $300; they had previously been making $45 a week at the gas station.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Andretti%E2%80%932016-14) From 1960 to 1961, Mario won 21 out of 46 [modified stock car](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modified_racing "Modified racing") races.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Bantam%E2%80%931970-18):37 The twins raced against each other only once, at [Oswego Speedway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oswego_Speedway "Oswego Speedway") in 1967; Mario won, with Aldo finishing tenth after a brake failure.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Comiskey%E2%80%932017-9)

To intimidate their opponents, the twins bought Italian racing suits and fabricated a story about racing in junior formulae back in Italy. Andretti maintained the fiction for many years.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Bantam%E2%80%931970-18):10–11[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-texaco-27)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-NSCHoF-4) In 2016, he admitted that the story was fabricated. He recalled that it "psych[ed] [the opponents] out, big time."[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Andretti%E2%80%932016-14)

### Single-seater racing

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mario_Andretti&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Single-seater racing")]

Despite his early successes in modified stock cars, Andretti's goal was to race in single-seater [open-wheel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open_wheel_racing "Open wheel racing") cars.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-NSCHoF-4) He started by racing [midget cars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midget_car_racing "Midget car racing") in the [American Racing Drivers Club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Racing_Drivers_Club "American Racing Drivers Club") (ARDC) series from 1961 to 1963, starting with 3/4 (sized) midgets before graduating to full-sized midgets.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-NSCHoF-4) In March 1962, he won a midget race, which he dubbed "my first victory of any consequence."[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Bantam%E2%80%931970-18):45 He raced in over one hundred events in 1963,[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-8W-28) and scored 29 top-five finishes in 46 ARDC races.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Malsher-Lopez%E2%80%932015-29) He finished third in the 1963 ARDC season standings.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-O'Leary%E2%80%932002-30):17 On [Labor Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Labor_Day "Labor Day") in 1963, Andretti won three feature races at two different tracks, an afternoon race at [Flemington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flemington,_New_Jersey "Flemington, New Jersey") and a doubleheader at [Hatfield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hatfield,_Pennsylvania "Hatfield, Pennsylvania"), after which reporter [Chris Economaki](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Economaki "Chris Economaki") told him that "you just bought the ticket to the big time."[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-NSCHoF-4)

From midget cars, the next step on the East Coast racing ladder was [sprint car racing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sprint_car_racing "Sprint car racing"), first with the United Racing Club (URC) series and then with the [United States Auto Club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Auto_Club "United States Auto Club") (USAC) series. Andretti attempted to secure a full-time URC ride, but received only spot starts. However, USAC team owner Rufus Gray gave him a full-time drive for 1964.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-NSCHoF-4) He won one race at [Salem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salem_Speedway "Salem Speedway") and finished third in the season standings behind veterans [Don Branson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Branson "Don Branson") and [Jud Larson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jud_Larson "Jud Larson").[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-USAC_National_Sprint_Car_Feature_Winners-31)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-USAC_National_Sprint_Car_Standings-32) To cover his expenses, he worked as a foreman at a golf cart factory.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Bantam%E2%80%931970-18):60

Andretti continued to race in sprint cars after progressing to IndyCar. In 1965 he won once at [Ascot Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ascot_Park_(speedway) "Ascot Park (speedway)"),[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-USAC_National_Sprint_Car_Feature_Winners-31) and finished tenth in the season standings.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-USAC_National_Sprint_Car_Standings-32) In 1966 he won five times ([Cumberland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cumberland,_Maryland "Cumberland, Maryland"), [Oswego](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oswego_Speedway "Oswego Speedway"), [Rossburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eldora_Speedway "Eldora Speedway"), Salem, and [Phoenix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manzanita_Speedway "Manzanita Speedway")),[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-USAC_National_Sprint_Car_Feature_Winners-31) but finished second in the standings, behind [Roger McCluskey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_McCluskey "Roger McCluskey").[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-USAC_National_Sprint_Car_Standings-32) In 1967 he won two of the three events that he entered.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-O'Leary%E2%80%932002-30):26

## USAC IndyCar career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mario_Andretti&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: USAC IndyCar career")]

From 1956 to 1978, the top [open-wheel racing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open-wheel_racing "Open-wheel racing") series in North America was the [USAC National Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USAC_National_Championship "USAC National Championship"), alternatively referred to as [IndyCar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IndyCar "IndyCar") or [Champ Car](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Champ_cars "Champ cars").[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-IndyCar_split_and_reunification-33) In [1971](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1971_USAC_Championship_Car_season "1971 USAC Championship Car season"), USAC split off its dirt-track races into a separate National Dirt Car Championship. The pavement championship retained the name [USAC Championship Car Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Auto_Club#USAC_Championship_Car_Series "United States Auto Club"), while the dirt championship had fewer races and was later rebranded to the "[Silver Crown Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Auto_Club#USAC_Silver_Crown_Series "United States Auto Club")."[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-34)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-O'Leary%E2%80%932002-30):50

### Breaking in (1964)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mario_Andretti&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Breaking in (1964)")]

Andretti entered IndyCar during the [1964](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1964_USAC_Championship_Car_season "1964 USAC Championship Car season") season, while still racing full-time in sprint cars. On April 19, 1964, the Doug Stearly team gave him a spot start at the [1964 Trenton 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trenton_150 "Trenton 150").[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-ESPN-26)[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-35) He started 16th and finished 11th.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Malsher-Lopez%E2%80%932015-29)

Andretti spent the first portion of the 1964 season trying to find a full-time IndyCar drive. An opening appeared to materialize when one of the big three IndyCar teams,[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-36) Dean Van Lines Racing Division (DVL), lost [Chuck Hulse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chuck_Hulse "Chuck Hulse") to injury.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Malsher-Lopez%E2%80%932015-29) Andretti met with DVL's chief mechanic, Clint Brawner, to ask for the drive. Although Andretti had come with an introduction from his sprint car team owner, Rufus Gray, Brawner turned Andretti down, as he was skeptical of sprint car racing and felt that Andretti was not ready to compete.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-NSCHoF-4)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Malsher-Lopez%E2%80%932015-29) He hired [Bob Mathouser](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Mathouser "Bob Mathouser") to replace Hulse.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Malsher-Lopez%E2%80%932015-29) Andretti joined Lee Glessner's outfit, but was forced to sit out the [1964 Indianapolis 500](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1964_Indianapolis_500 "1964 Indianapolis 500").[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Malsher-Lopez%E2%80%932015-29)

### Dean Van Lines, Andretti Racing, and STP (1964–1971)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mario_Andretti&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Dean Van Lines, Andretti Racing, and STP (1964–1971)")]

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f9/Mario_Andretti_en_1970.jpg/250px-Mario_Andretti_en_1970.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Mario_Andretti_en_1970.jpg)

Andretti in 1970.

Andretti got his big break with DVL midway through the 1964 season, after the youngster impressed Brawner in two races: a sprint car race in [Terre Haute, Indiana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terre_Haute,_Indiana "Terre Haute, Indiana")[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-NSCHoF-4) and an IndyCar race at [Langhorne Speedway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Langhorne_Speedway "Langhorne Speedway"), where Andretti finished ninth, just three places below Mathouser, who had the better car.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-37)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Bantam%E2%80%931970-18):78–80 Brawner had mentored a young [A. J. Foyt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A._J._Foyt "A. J. Foyt"), and noticed that Andretti "worked as diligently on the car as Foyt had as a rookie with me."[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Indy_500_Mechanic-38):130 Andretti was pleased to join what he called one of the "few outfits worth driving for."[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-39) He completed the final eight races of the season with DVL,[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-40) finishing 11th in the season standings.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-41) He was named [IndyCar Rookie of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IndyCar_Rookie_of_the_Year "IndyCar Rookie of the Year").[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-42) After the season, Brawner agreed to make Andretti his permanent driver in place of Hulse.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Bantam%E2%80%931970-18):97–98

#### 1965–1969: Years of domination

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mario_Andretti&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: 1965–1969: Years of domination")]

The Andretti-Brawner combination would soon come to dominate the sport. It quickly attracted technical and financial support from [Firestone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Firestone_Tire_and_Rubber_Company "Firestone Tire and Rubber Company") and [Ford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ford_Motor_Company "Ford Motor Company"); Brawner said that Ford treated DVL like a [works team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Works_team "Works team").[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Indy_500_Mechanic-38):150,157 From 1965 to 1969, Andretti won three USAC IndyCar titles. He also came within 93 points of winning five in a row; for comparison, at the time, 100 points was the difference between [finishing sixth and seventh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_American_Championship_car_racing_points_scoring_systems#AAA_Championships_1946%E2%80%931955_and_USAC_Championships_1956%E2%80%931977 "List of American Championship car racing points scoring systems") at the Indianapolis 500. At the peak of his statistical dominance, Andretti won 29 of 85 USAC championship races between 1966 and 1969.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-sportscentury-8)

In [1965](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1965_USAC_Championship_Car_season "1965 USAC Championship Car season"), Andretti's first full season with DVL, he took advantage of the team's new [Brawner Hawk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brawner_Hawk "Brawner Hawk"), a derivation of the [Brabham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brabham "Brabham") Formula One chassis.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Malsher-Lopez%E2%80%932015-29) His third-place finish at the [1965 Indianapolis 500](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1965_Indianapolis_500 "1965 Indianapolis 500") earned him the race's [Rookie of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Indianapolis_500_Rookies_of_the_Year "List of Indianapolis 500 Rookies of the Year") award.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Malsher-Lopez%E2%80%932015-29) He won his first IndyCar race at the [Hoosier Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hoosier_Grand_Prix "Hoosier Grand Prix").[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-IMHoF-43) Although he won only one race that year, he scored six second places and three third places, and scored points in 16 out of 18 races.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-44) His closest competitor, A. J. Foyt (who had won four of the last five USAC titles) won five races but failed to score seven times.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-45) At age 25, Andretti became the youngest IndyCar champion in history,[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-8W-28) a record he held for thirty years until [Jacques Villeneuve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacques_Villeneuve "Jacques Villeneuve") won the [1995](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1995_PPG_Indy_Car_World_Series "1995 PPG Indy Car World Series") title.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Malsher-Lopez%E2%80%932015-29) To his irritation, however, when he appeared on [Johnny Carson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Tonight_Show_Starring_Johnny_Carson "The Tonight Show Starring Johnny Carson") at the end of the season, he was introduced as the Indy 500 Rookie of the Year, which he felt downplayed his title win.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Malsher-Lopez%E2%80%932015-29)[[d]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-48)

In [1966](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1966_USAC_Championship_Car_season "1966 USAC Championship Car season"), Andretti won his second straight USAC title. In contrast to his maiden title win, Andretti won eight of fifteen starts[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-49) and led 1,142 laps, nearly 1,000 laps more than his closest competitor.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Malsher-Lopez%E2%80%932015-29) He led 54.5% of all laps in 1966, a record until [Al Unser](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Unser "Al Unser")'s 66.8% in [1970](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1970_USAC_Championship_Car_season "1970 USAC Championship Car season"), and still the second-highest figure in history as of the 2022 season.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Pryson%E2%80%932022-50) Andretti also took pole at the [1966 Indianapolis 500](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1966_Indianapolis_500 "1966 Indianapolis 500"), but retired after 27 laps with a mechanical failure.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Indianapolis_500_Career-51)

In [1967](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1967_USAC_Championship_Car_season "1967 USAC Championship Car season"), Andretti lost the season USAC championship to A. J. Foyt. Although Andretti won eight races, Foyt won the [1967 Indianapolis 500](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1967_Indianapolis_500 "1967 Indianapolis 500");[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Andretti_vs_Foyt-52) Andretti was on pole at Indianapolis but lost a wheel.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Andretti_vs_Foyt_&_Petty-53) Andretti fought through broken ribs to stay in the title race.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Andretti_vs_Foyt_&_Petty-53) Foyt carried a 340-point lead over Andretti going into the season-ending [Rex Mays 300](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Budweiser_500K "Budweiser 500K") at [Riverside](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverside_International_Raceway "Riverside International Raceway").[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Andretti_vs_Foyt_&_Petty-53) Andretti ran out of fuel with four laps to go and settled for third,[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Andretti_vs_Foyt_&_Petty-53) costing him 180 points.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-1967_Rex_Mays_300-54) Ordinarily, he would have won the championship anyway, as third place was worth 420 points and Foyt had crashed on lap 50.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-1967_Rex_Mays_300-54) However, Foyt's tire sponsor Goodyear arranged for him to commandeer [Roger McCluskey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_McCluskey "Roger McCluskey")'s car to prevent Andretti, a Firestone man, from winning.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Andretti_vs_Foyt_&_Petty-53)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Bantam%E2%80%931970-18):179–180 Foyt piloted McCluskey's car to fifth place. Despite a point deduction, he won the championship by 80 points.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-MSM%E2%80%93American_Comment-55) Andretti received his first [Driver of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Driver_of_the_Year "Driver of the Year") award but was deflated by how the season ended, saying, "I had the championship in my hands, and then it was gone."[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Andretti_vs_Foyt_&_Petty-53)

DVL owner Al Dean died at the end of the 1967 season. Per his wishes, the team was wound up. The estate sold the team's assets to Andretti, who became an owner-driver under the name Andretti Racing Enterprises.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Bantam%E2%80%931970-18):181–182 Brawner stayed on as chief mechanic.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-56) In [1968](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1968_USAC_Championship_Car_season "1968 USAC Championship Car season"), Andretti once again lost the title at the final race of the season at Riverside, but this time in a reversal of the events of 1967. Andretti held a 304-point lead over [Bobby Unser](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bobby_Unser "Bobby Unser") at the start and led Unser on track by 47 seconds at one point. However, his engine failed on lap 58. He borrowed [Joe Leonard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Leonard "Joe Leonard")'s car (whose brakes were dead[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Bantam%E2%80%931970-18):200) and then [Lloyd Ruby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lloyd_Ruby "Lloyd Ruby")'s car for the final stretch. He fought back to third, but received only 165 points instead of the usual 420 since only his laps in Ruby's car were counted.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-57) Unser finished second, scoring 480 points.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-MSM%E2%80%93American_Comment-55) Unser won the title by 11 points, the narrowest margin in USAC history.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Bantam%E2%80%931970-18):202 Despite losing the title, Andretti set records for second-place finishes in a season (11 times in 27 starts) and podium finishes in a season (16), which still stand to this day.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Pryson%E2%80%932022-50)

Granatelli retained the DVL cars and staff, although Brawner disliked Granatelli and insisted that he not participate in racing decisions.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Kravitz%E2%80%932021-59) Andretti won nine races in 1969, including the [1969 Indianapolis 500](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1969_Indianapolis_500 "1969 Indianapolis 500") and the [Pikes Peak International Hill Climb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pikes_Peak_International_Hill_Climb "Pikes Peak International Hill Climb").[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-ESPN-26) He won his third title and was named [ABC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Broadcasting_Company "American Broadcasting Company")'s [Wide World of Sports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wide_World_of_Sports_(U.S._TV_series) "Wide World of Sports (U.S. TV series)") Athlete of the Year.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-60) His 5,025 points were a USAC record, and he scored nearly twice as many points as runner-up [Al Unser](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Unser "Al Unser") (2,630).[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Andretti_vs_Foyt-52) His IndyCar prize money of $365,165 (including a $205,727 check for winning the Indianapolis 500) was, by one count, the largest single-season haul in the history of American sports to that point, and his total pay that year (including endorsements) was estimated at as much as $1 million.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-61)

#### 1970–1971: Team split and struggles

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mario_Andretti&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: 1970–1971: Team split and struggles")]

The core of the team split up after the 1969 title season, when Goodyear persuaded STP mechanics Clint Brawner and Jim McGee to start their own team.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Bantam%E2%80%931970-18):206 Andretti remained with STP, which agreed to sponsor him during the [1970 Formula One season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1970_Formula_One_season "1970 Formula One season") in a privateer [March](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/March_Engineering "March Engineering").[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-62)

Various reasons were given for the split. Brawner said that he and McGee left because Granatelli and Firestone were underpaying them, and added that his old-school thinking clashed with Andretti and McGee's desire to innovate.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Indy_500_Mechanic-38):164–166 He was particularly hurt that Andretti wanted to retire the old Brawner Hawk for a chassis from [Lotus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Lotus "Team Lotus").[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Indy_500_Mechanic-38):167–168 However, it was also rumored that Andretti forced out Brawner, which Andretti denied.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Miller%E2%80%932020-58) In his foreword to Brawner's 1975 autobiography, Andretti wrote that "we had our disagreements, but until things started turning sour near the end, we worked them out."[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Indy_500_Mechanic-38):xii He added that "there are many reasons why our operation fell apart. ... Racing relationships are like Hollywood marriages: they seldom last long."[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Indy_500_Mechanic-38):xiv McGee said that Andretti and Brawner had been "feuding for years,"[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Glick%E2%80%931994-63) but "certainly respected each other."[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Miller%E2%80%932020-58) He opined that Brawner was unwilling to work for Granatelli.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Glick%E2%80%931994-63) According to an [urban legend](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urban_legend "Urban legend"), Brawner's wife Kay hexed Andretti's family after the STP split, giving rise to the so-called "[Andretti curse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andretti_curse "Andretti curse")."[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Miller%E2%80%932020-58)

Neither side fully recovered from the split. The Brawner/McGee team's financial backer went broke, and McGee returned to STP in 1971.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Indy_500_Mechanic-38):175–176 Meanwhile, Andretti settled for a fifth-place finish in [1970](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1970_USAC_Championship_Car_season "1970 USAC Championship Car season"),[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Racing%E2%80%93Reference-64) and the STP Formula One team shut down after one season.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-65) In [1971](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1971_USAC_Championship_Car_season "1971 USAC Championship Car season"), Andretti fell to ninth in USAC's paved track championship.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Racing%E2%80%93Reference-64) He scored no points in the [dirt track standings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1971_USAC_National_Dirt_Car_Championship "1971 USAC National Dirt Car Championship"), with a best finish of 13th.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-O'Leary%E2%80%932002-30):45

### Parnelli (1972–1975)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mario_Andretti&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Parnelli (1972–1975)")]

For the [1972](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1971_USAC_Championship_Car_season "1971 USAC Championship Car season") season, Andretti left STP and joined [Vel's Parnelli Jones Racing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vel's_Parnelli_Jones_Racing "Vel's Parnelli Jones Racing").[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-66) Parnelli was IndyCar's dominant team at the time, with 1970 champion [Al Unser](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Unser "Al Unser") and 1971 champion [Joe Leonard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Leonard "Joe Leonard").[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Sports_Illustrated%E2%80%931978-67) Andretti persuaded the team to hire Lotus designer [Maurice Philippe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maurice_Philippe "Maurice Philippe"),[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-O'Keefe%E2%80%932003-68) and Jim McGee also joined the team.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Glick%E2%80%931994-63) The combination was expected to be a "superteam."[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-69)[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Lerner%E2%80%932021-70)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-O'Leary%E2%80%932002-30):52

Andretti never won an IndyCar title with Parnelli.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Sports_Illustrated%E2%80%931978-67) In his three full-time IndyCar seasons with the team (1972–1974), Andretti finished 11th, 5th, and 14th,[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Racing%E2%80%93Reference-64) while his teammate Leonard won the [1972](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1972_USAC_Championship_Car_season "1972 USAC Championship Car season") title.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-O'Leary%E2%80%932002-30):48 He did better on dirt tracks, winning the 1974 title after winning three out of five races.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-SilverCrownStandings-71)[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-SilverCrownWinners-72) He nearly won the 1973 title as well, but teammate Al Unser beat him even though Andretti won two out of three races.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-SilverCrownStandings-71)[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-SilverCrownWinners-72)[[e]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-73)

During this period, Andretti was increasingly drawn to [formula racing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Formula_racing "Formula racing"). He made guest appearances in [Formula One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Formula_One "Formula One") with [Ferrari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scuderia_Ferrari "Scuderia Ferrari") in [1972](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1972_Formula_One_season "1972 Formula One season"),[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Formula_One%E2%80%931972-74) and raced in [Formula 5000](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Formula_5000 "Formula 5000") in [1974](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1974_SCCA/USAC_Formula_5000_Championship "1974 SCCA/USAC Formula 5000 Championship") and [1975](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1975_SCCA/USAC_Formula_5000_Championship "1975 SCCA/USAC Formula 5000 Championship").[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Kirby%E2%80%932013-75) In 1975, Andretti stopped competing full-time in IndyCar,[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Mario_Andretti_Results-76) instead driving full-time for the Parnelli Formula One team.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Francis%E2%80%932025-77) After quitting Formula One in early 1976,[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-O'Keefe%E2%80%932003_part_2-78) Parnelli released Andretti from his USAC contract so that he could focus on Formula One.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-79)

### Penske (1976–1978)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mario_Andretti&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Penske (1976–1978)")]

While racing with [Team Lotus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Lotus "Team Lotus"), Andretti appeared sporadically in IndyCar with McGee's new team, [Penske Racing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penske_Racing "Penske Racing").[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Glick%E2%80%931994-63) In nineteen races from 1976 to 1978, he won one race (at [Trenton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trenton_Speedway "Trenton Speedway") in 1978) and collected eight top-five finishes.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Racing%E2%80%93Reference-64)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-O'Leary%E2%80%932002-30):66

## Stock car racing career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mario_Andretti&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Stock car racing career")]

At the height of his IndyCar career, Andretti also made thirty appearances in top-level [stock car racing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stock_car_racing "Stock car racing") from 1965 to 1969. Along with [A. J. Foyt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A._J._Foyt "A. J. Foyt"), he is one of two drivers to ever win [NASCAR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASCAR "NASCAR")'s most prestigious race, the [Daytona 500](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daytona_500 "Daytona 500"), without being a full-time stock car driver.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Oreovicz%E2%80%932017-80)

In USAC, Andretti scored one win and eight top-five finishes in sixteen races from 1965 to 1968.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-O'Leary%E2%80%932002-30):21,25,27,31 His best season performance was 1967, when he competed in eight out of 22 races,[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-81) won round 12 at [Mosport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mosport "Mosport"),[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-82) and finished seventh in the standings.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-83)

In the NASCAR [Grand National Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASCAR_Cup_Series "NASCAR Cup Series"), Andretti was less successful on average, with one win, one top-five finish, and three top tens in fourteen races from 1966 to 1969.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Mario_Andretti_Results-76) He primarily drove for Ford works team [Holman-Moody](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holman-Moody "Holman-Moody"), securing the drive through his connections at Ford headquarters.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Sabotage-84) He generally did not get the first pick of equipment and pit crews,[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Jensen%E2%80%932020-85) and said that a lack of technical support forced him to ask a rookie, [Donnie Allison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donnie_Allison "Donnie Allison"), for help setting up his car.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-1967Daytona500-86)[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Sabotage-84)_[Sports Illustrated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sports\_Illustrated "Sports Illustrated")_ noted that Andretti's setup favored [oversteer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oversteer "Oversteer") (in American parlance, "loose"[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-87)) to an extent that was considered extreme at the time.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Sports_Illustrated%E2%80%931978-67) After convincing the team to give him a top-spec engine,[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Jensen%E2%80%932020-85) he won the [1967 Daytona 500](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1967_Daytona_500 "1967 Daytona 500"), but alleged that the team tried to sabotage his race so that its lead driver, [Fred Lorenzen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fred_Lorenzen "Fred Lorenzen"), could inherit the win.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Jensen%E2%80%932020-85)[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-1967Daytona500-86) His friend [Parnelli Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parnelli_Jones "Parnelli Jones") backed up the accusation.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Oreovicz%E2%80%932017-80) Andretti stopped competing in NASCAR after 1969, as race seats at teams of the caliber of Holman-Moody rarely came open after the 1960s.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-88)

In the 1970s and 1980s, Andretti competed in six editions of the [International Race of Champions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Race_of_Champions "International Race of Champions") (IROC), an invitational stock car series with a limited calendar. ### Part-time roles (1968–1970)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mario_Andretti&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Part-time roles (1968–1970)")]

[![Image 14](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f4/AndrettiMario19690801Lotus63-Allrad-3.jpg/250px-AndrettiMario19690801Lotus63-Allrad-3.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:AndrettiMario19690801Lotus63-Allrad-3.jpg)

Andretti driving the [Lotus 63](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lotus_63 "Lotus 63") at the [1969 German Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1969_German_Grand_Prix "1969 German Grand Prix").

Although the [Indianapolis 500](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indianapolis_500 "Indianapolis 500") dropped off the Formula One calendar in 1960, some teams continued racing at Indianapolis, including [Colin Chapman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colin_Chapman "Colin Chapman")'s [Team Lotus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Lotus "Team Lotus").[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-89) At the [1965 Indianapolis 500](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1965_Indianapolis_500 "1965 Indianapolis 500"), Lotus star [Jim Clark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Clark "Jim Clark") won and Andretti finished third as the top-placed rookie.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-FormulaOneBio-90)[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Taylor%E2%80%932007-91) On Clark's recommendation,[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Hughes%E2%80%932020-92) Chapman invited Andretti to race in Formula One, saying, "When you're ready, call me."[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Taylor%E2%80%932007-91)[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Vaughn%E2%80%932019-93)

Andretti joined Lotus for the [1968 Italian Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1968_Italian_Grand_Prix "1968 Italian Grand Prix").[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-MSM%E2%80%932016-94) He was delighted by the [Lotus 49B](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lotus_49 "Lotus 49"), saying that its handling was a major improvement over IndyCar.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Hughes%E2%80%932020-92) He beat the [Monza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monza_Circuit "Monza Circuit") lap record in testing,[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-MSM%E2%80%932016-94) but was disqualified after flying back to America for a contractually required race.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-MSM%E2%80%932016-94) He later said that the Monza officials broke a promise to waive the applicable rule on his behalf.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-95)[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Vaughn%E2%80%932019-93)

Andretti got his real start in Formula One at the [1968 United States Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1968_United_States_Grand_Prix "1968 United States Grand Prix") and took pole.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-FormulaOneBio-90)[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-96) Due to his disqualification at Monza (where he had qualified tenth),[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-97) he became the first Formula One driver to start his first race from pole.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Hughes%E2%80%932020-92)[Jackie Stewart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jackie_Stewart "Jackie Stewart") overtook him on the first lap, but the two drivers were neck-and-neck until Andretti's nose cone broke, forcing him to pit. He eventually retired with a clutch failure, but he had made a strong impression. Reviewing the race _, [Motor Sport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motor\_Sport\_(magazine) "Motor Sport (magazine)")_ wrote that Andretti displayed "that same assurance of absolute control [in the corners] one saw in [Jim] Clark's driving."[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-98)

> It's my neck. I put it under the guillotine every time I climb into a race car. So if somebody puts a price on it, I am going to study the sales tag—very carefully.

—Mario Andretti,_What's it Like Out There?_[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Bantam%E2%80%931970-18):151

At the end of the 1968 season, Chapman offered Andretti a full-time drive to replace Clark, who had died in [an accident](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1968_Deutschland_Troph%C3%A4e "1968 Deutschland Trophäe") that April. Andretti declined, not wishing to give up his stable USAC career. For the next two years, he made only sporadic appearances in Formula One with Lotus and [STP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STP_(motor_oil_company) "STP (motor oil company)")-[March](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/March_Engineering "March Engineering").[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-FormulaOneBio-90) The cars were mostly uncompetitive, and he finished only one race in his first three seasons.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-O'Leary%E2%80%932002-30):42 At the one race he finished, the [1970 Spanish Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1970_Spanish_Grand_Prix "1970 Spanish Grand Prix"), he collected his first Formula One podium after several drivers ahead of him retired with mechanical issues.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-99)

### Ferrari (1971–1972)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mario_Andretti&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: Ferrari (1971–1972)")]

Andretti signed with [Scuderia Ferrari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scuderia_Ferrari "Scuderia Ferrari") in [1971](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1971_Formula_One_season "1971 Formula One season") and entered seven out of 11 races, completing two. In his Ferrari debut, he achieved his maiden Grand Prix win at [Kyalami](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1971_South_African_Grand_Prix "1971 South African Grand Prix") after race leader [Denny Hulme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denny_Hulme "Denny Hulme")'s engine failed with four laps to go.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-100) He also won the non-championship [Questor Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1971_Questor_Grand_Prix "1971 Questor Grand Prix") in California. Following the Questor win, [Enzo Ferrari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enzo_Ferrari "Enzo Ferrari") offered to make Andretti his No. 1 driver for 1972, but Andretti declined, later remarking that "[Formula One] didn't pay much back then [...] but I always figured I'd get another opportunity."[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Ferrari1971-101) Andretti also raced five times in [1972](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1972_Formula_One_season "1972 Formula One season"), but scored no podiums.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Formula_One%E2%80%931972-74) He did not compete in the [1973](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1973_Formula_One_season "1973 Formula One season") season.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-102)

### Parnelli (1974–1976)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mario_Andretti&action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: Parnelli (1974–1976)")]

In the mid-1970s, Andretti encouraged [Parnelli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vel's_Parnelli_Jones_Racing "Vel's Parnelli Jones Racing"), his IndyCar team, to sponsor a Formula One car.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Blackstock%E2%80%932024-103) To prepare for a Formula One challenge, the team secured funding from [Firestone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Firestone_Tire_and_Rubber_Company "Firestone Tire and Rubber Company"),[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Blackstock%E2%80%932024-103)[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Vaughn%E2%80%932019-93) which agreed to make special tires for the team.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Lerner%E2%80%932021-70) In addition to Maurice Philippe, the team hired more Lotus veterans, including Jim Clark's old crew chief Dick Scammell and administrator Andrew Ferguson.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-O'Keefe%E2%80%932003-68)

Parnelli ran Andretti in the two North American end-of-season races in [1974](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1974_Formula_One_season "1974 Formula One season").[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Vaughn%E2%80%932019-93) He qualified third at the [United States Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1974_United_States_Grand_Prix "1974 United States Grand Prix") but did not start the race due to a mechanical failure.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-O'Keefe%E2%80%932003-68)[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Lerner%E2%80%932021-70) Parnelli also ran Andretti in the North American [Formula 5000](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Formula_5000 "Formula 5000") series in [1974](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1974_SCCA/USAC_Formula_5000_Championship "1974 SCCA/USAC Formula 5000 Championship") and [1975](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1975_SCCA/USAC_Formula_5000_Championship "1975 SCCA/USAC Formula 5000 Championship"), both times finishing second to [Brian Redman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brian_Redman "Brian Redman").[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Kirby%E2%80%932013-75) In each season, Andretti won as many races as Redman, but his results were less consistent.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-O'Leary%E2%80%932002-30):52–56

In [1975](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1975_Formula_One_season "1975 Formula One season"), Andretti became a full-time Formula One driver for the first time.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Francis%E2%80%932025-77) He was disappointed by the [Parnelli VPJ4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parnelli_VPJ4 "Parnelli VPJ4"), which he felt was derivative of the [Lotus 72](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lotus_72 "Lotus 72"). More importantly, sponsor Firestone pulled out ahead of the season.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-O'Keefe%E2%80%932003-68) The VPJ4 had been designed for Firestone's custom tires, and without them, its performance suffered.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Lerner%E2%80%932021-70) The car also suffered from frequent brake failures.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-O'Keefe%E2%80%932003_part_2-78) At the [Spanish Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1975_Spanish_Grand_Prix "1975 Spanish Grand Prix"), Andretti qualified fourth and reached first after a multi-car crash on the first lap. However, the crash damaged his suspension, forcing his eventual retirement.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-104) He finished third at the non-championship [1975 BRDC International Trophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1975_BRDC_International_Trophy "1975 BRDC International Trophy") Race.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-O'Keefe%E2%80%932003-68) At the [Swedish Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1975_Swedish_Grand_Prix "1975 Swedish Grand Prix"), he was nearly killed when his brakes failed during qualifying, but finished fourth with the team's backup car.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Lerner%E2%80%932021-70) He finished 14th in the Drivers' Championship, scoring five points.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-105)

Parnelli skipped the first race of the [1976 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1976_Formula_One_season "1976 Formula One season"),[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-O'Keefe%E2%80%932003_part_2-78) so Andretti started the year with Lotus and returned to Parnelli for the next two races.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-106)[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Vaughn%E2%80%932019-93) Parnelli pulled out of Formula One after round three when sponsor [Viceroy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viceroy_(cigarette) "Viceroy (cigarette)") withdrew funding.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-8W-28) Andretti only learned of the decision when a reporter asked him about it as the grid lined up to start the race.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-O'Keefe%E2%80%932003_part_2-78)[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Lerner%E2%80%932021-70) He later admitted that "I was the only one, really, that wanted [the Formula One team]."[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti#cite_note-Vaughn%E2%80%932019-93)

The Saint Peter's Square is the heart of the Greek city of [Argos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Argos,_Peloponnese "Argos, Peloponnese").

A **town square** (or **public square**, **urban square**, **city square** or simply **square**), also called a **plaza** or **piazza**, is an open [public space](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_space "Public space") commonly found in the heart of a traditional [town](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Town "Town") or [city](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City "City"), and which may sometimes be used for community gatherings. Related concepts are the [civic center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Civic_center "Civic center"), the [market square](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Market_square "Market square") and the [village green](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Village_green "Village green").

Most squares are [hardscapes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hardscape "Hardscape") suitable for open [markets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Market_(place) "Market (place)"), [concerts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Concert "Concert"), political rallies, and other events that require firm ground. They are not necessarily a true [geometric square](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Square "Square").

Being centrally located, town squares are often surrounded by small shops such as bakeries, meat markets, cheese stores, and clothing stores. At their center is often a [well](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Well "Well"), [monument](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monument "Monument"), [statue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue "Statue") or other feature. Those with fountains are sometimes called fountain squares.

The term "town square" (especially via the term "public square") is synonymous with the politics of many cultures, and the names of a certain town squares, such as the [Euromaidan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euromaidan "Euromaidan") and [Red Square](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Square "Red Square"), have become symbolic of specific political events throughout history.

## Australia

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Town_square&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Australia")]

Many cities in Australia's eastern states, such as [Melbourne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Melbourne "Melbourne") and [Sydney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sydney "Sydney"), did not have a central town square in their design, due to a fear of rebellion. [New South Wales Governors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governor_of_New_South_Wales "Governor of New South Wales")[Richard Bourke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Bourke "Richard Bourke") and [George Gipps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Gipps "George Gipps") notably ordered surveyors to not include a town square in city designs, including Melbourne, to prevent the spirit of democracy from arising.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piazza#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piazza#cite_note-2)

The [city centre of Adelaide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adelaide_city_centre "Adelaide city centre") and the adjacent suburb of [North Adelaide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Adelaide "North Adelaide"), in [South Australia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Australia "South Australia"), were planned by [Colonel William Light](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colonel_William_Light "Colonel William Light") in 1837. The city streets were laid out in a [grid plan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grid_plan "Grid plan"), with the city centre including a central public square, [Victoria Square](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victoria_Square,_Adelaide "Victoria Square, Adelaide"), and four public squares in the centre of each quarter of the city. North Adelaide has two public squares. The city was also designed to be surrounded by [park lands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adelaide_park_lands "Adelaide park lands"), and all of these features still exist today, with the squares maintained as mostly green spaces.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piazza#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piazza#cite_note-4)

In 2025, the [City of Sydney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_of_Sydney "City of Sydney") council approved plans to accelerate the construction of a public square near the current [Town Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sydney_Town_Hall "Sydney Town Hall").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piazza#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piazza#cite_note-6)

## China

In China, [People's Square](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People's_Square_(disambiguation) "People's Square (disambiguation)") is a common designation for the central town square of modern Chinese cities, established as part of urban modernization within the last few decades. These squares are the site of government buildings, museums, and other public buildings. One such square, [Tiananmen Square](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tiananmen_Square "Tiananmen Square"), is a famous site in Chinese history due to it being the site of the [May Fourth Movement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/May_Fourth_Movement "May Fourth Movement"), the [Proclamation of the People's Republic of China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proclamation_of_the_People's_Republic_of_China "Proclamation of the People's Republic of China"), the [1976 Tiananmen Incident](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1976_Tiananmen_Incident "1976 Tiananmen Incident"), the [1989 Tiananmen Square Protests](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1989_Tiananmen_Square_Protests "1989 Tiananmen Square Protests"), and all [Chinese National Day Parades](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_National_Day_Parade "Chinese National Day Parade").

[![Image 10](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/46/Neues_Schloss_Schlossplatzspringbrunnen_Jubil%C3%A4umss%C3%A4ule_Schlossplatz_Stuttgart_2015_02.jpg/250px-Neues_Schloss_Schlossplatzspringbrunnen_Jubil%C3%A4umss%C3%A4ule_Schlossplatz_Stuttgart_2015_02.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Neues_Schloss_Schlossplatzspringbrunnen_Jubil%C3%A4umss%C3%A4ule_Schlossplatz_Stuttgart_2015_02.jpg)

[Schlossplatz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schlossplatz_(Stuttgart) "Schlossplatz (Stuttgart)") in [Stuttgart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stuttgart "Stuttgart"), Germany

The German word for square is _Platz_, which also means "Place", and is a common term for open spaces (not necessarily square) in German-speaking countries. Some of these have been focal points of public life in towns and cities from the Middle Ages to today. Squares located opposite a palace or castle ([German](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_language "German language"): _[Schloss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schloss "Schloss")_) are commonly named [Schlossplatz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schlossplatz_(disambiguation) "Schlossplatz (disambiguation)"). Prominent _Plätze_ include the [Alexanderplatz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexanderplatz "Alexanderplatz"), [Pariser Platz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pariser_Platz "Pariser Platz") and [Potsdamer Platz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Potsdamer_Platz "Potsdamer Platz") in Berlin, the [Heldenplatz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heldenplatz "Heldenplatz") in Vienna, and the [Königsplatz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K%C3%B6nigsplatz,_Munich "Königsplatz, Munich") in Munich.
