In traditional Persian architecture, town squares are known as maydan or meydan. A maydan is considered one of the essential features in urban planning and they are often adjacent to bazaars, large mosques and other public buildings. [Naqsh-e Jahan Square](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naqsh-e_Jahan_Square "Naqsh-e Jahan Square") in Isfahan and [Azadi Square](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Azadi_Square "Azadi Square") in Tehran are examples of classic and modern squares.

## Italy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Town_square&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Italy")]

"Piazza" redirects here. For other uses, see [Piazza (disambiguation)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piazza_(disambiguation) "Piazza (disambiguation)").

[![Image 13](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/25/Piazza_Navona_1.jpg/250px-Piazza_Navona_1.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Piazza_Navona_1.jpg)

[Piazza Navona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piazza_Navona "Piazza Navona") and the [Fontana del Moro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fontana_del_Moro "Fontana del Moro") in [Rome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rome "Rome"), Italy. The fountain in the foreground is [Fontana dei Quattro Fiumi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fontana_dei_Quattro_Fiumi "Fontana dei Quattro Fiumi").

A _**piazza**_ (Italian pronunciation:[[ˈpjattsa]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Italian "Help:IPA/Italian")) is a [city square](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_square "City square") in [Italy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italy "Italy"), [Malta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malta "Malta"), along the [Dalmatian coast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalmatian_coast "Dalmatian coast") and in surrounding regions. Possibly influenced by the centrality of the [Roman forum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forum_(Roman) "Forum (Roman)") to ancient Mediterranean culture, the _piazze_ of Italy are central to most towns and cities. Shops, businesses, metro stations, and bus stops are commonly found on _piazzas_, and in multiple locations also feature [Roman Catholic churches](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roman_Catholic_churches "Roman Catholic churches"), such as in places known as the [Piazza del Duomo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piazza_del_Duomo_(disambiguation) "Piazza del Duomo (disambiguation)"), with the most famous perhaps being [the one in Milan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piazza_del_Duomo,_Milan "Piazza del Duomo, Milan"), or government buildings, such as the Piazza del Quirinale adjacent to the [Quirinal Palace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quirinal_Palace "Quirinal Palace") of the [Italian president](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_Italy "President of Italy") in Rome.

The [Piazza San Marco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piazza_San_Marco "Piazza San Marco") in [Venice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venice "Venice") and [Piazza del Popolo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piazza_del_Popolo "Piazza del Popolo") in Rome are among the world's best known Italian _piazzas_. These squares historically played a major role in the political developments of Italy in both the [Italian Medieval era](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italy_in_the_Middle_Ages "Italy in the Middle Ages") and the [Italian Renaissance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_Renaissance "Italian Renaissance").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piazza#cite_note-11) For example, the [Piazza della Signoria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piazza_della_Signoria "Piazza della Signoria") in [Florence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florence "Florence") remains synonymous with the return of the [Medici](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medici "Medici") from their exile in 1530 as well as the burning at the stake of [Savonarola](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Girolamo_Savonarola "Girolamo Savonarola").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piazza#cite_note-12)[Naples](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naples "Naples")' main square is [Piazza del Plebiscito](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piazza_del_Plebiscito "Piazza del Plebiscito").

The Italian term is roughly equivalent to the Spanish _[plaza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plaza "Plaza")_, French term _place_, Portuguese _praça_, and German _Platz_. The concept should not be confused with an unrelated usage of the term referring to a feature of architectural or urban design, such as the _piazza_ at [King's Cross station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London_King's_Cross_railway_station "London King's Cross railway station") in London or _piazza_ as a [verandah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Verandah "Verandah") or front [porch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Porch "Porch") of a house or apartment in the United States,[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piazza#cite_note-13) such as at [George Washington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Washington "George Washington")'s historic home [Mount Vernon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mount_Vernon "Mount Vernon").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piazza#cite_note-14)

Several countries, especially around the [Mediterranean Sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mediterranean_Sea "Mediterranean Sea"), feature Italian-style town squares. In Gibraltar, one such town square just off [Gibraltar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gibraltar "Gibraltar")'s [Main Street](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Main_Street,_Gibraltar "Main Street, Gibraltar"), between the [Parliament Building](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gibraltar_Parliament "Gibraltar Parliament") and the [City Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gibraltar_City_Hall "Gibraltar City Hall") officially named _[John Mackintosh Square](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John\_Mackintosh\_Square "John Mackintosh Square")_ is referred to as _The Piazza_.

## Netherlands and Belgium

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Town_square&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Netherlands and Belgium")]

[![Image 14](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f5/Grote_Markt_%289379072012%29.jpg/250px-Grote_Markt_%289379072012%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Grote_Markt_(9379072012).jpg)

[Grand-Place](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand-Place "Grand-Place") in [Brussels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels "Brussels"), Belgium

In the [Low Countries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Low_Countries "Low Countries"), squares are often called "markets" because of their usage as [marketplaces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marketplace "Marketplace"). Most towns and cities in Belgium and the southern part of the Netherlands have in their historical centre a _Grote Markt_ (literally "Big Market") in Dutch or _Grand-Place_ (literally "Grand Square") in French[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piazza#cite_note-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piazza#cite_note-16) (for example the [Grand-Place](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand-Place "Grand-Place") in [Brussels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels "Brussels") and the _[Grote Markt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grote\_Markt\_(Antwerp) "Grote Markt (Antwerp)")_ in [Antwerp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antwerp "Antwerp")). The _Grote Markt_ or _Grand-Place_ is often the location of the [town hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Town_hall "Town hall"), hence also the political centre of the town. The Dutch word for square is _plein_, which is another common name for squares in Dutch-speaking regions (for example [Het Plein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Het_Plein "Het Plein") in [The Hague](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Hague "The Hague")).

In the 17th and 18th centuries, another type of square emerged, the so-called _royal square_ (French: _Place royale_, Dutch: _Koningsplein_). Such squares did not serve as a marketplace but were built in front of large palaces or public buildings to emphasise their grandeur, as well as to accommodate [military parades](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_parade "Military parade") and ceremonies, among others (for example the [Place Royale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Place_Royale,_Brussels "Place Royale, Brussels") in Brussels and the [Koningsplein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koningsplein "Koningsplein") in [Amsterdam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amsterdam "Amsterdam")). Palace squares are usually more symmetrical than their older market counterparts.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piazza#cite_note-17)

In Russia, _central square_ ([Russian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_language "Russian language"): центра́льная пло́щадь, [romanised](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romanization_of_Russian "Romanization of Russian"): _tsentráĺnaya plóshchad́_) is a common term for an open area in the heart of the [town](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Town "Town").[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] In a number of cities, the square has no individual name and is officially designated _Central Square_, for example [Central Square (Tolyatti)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Square_(Tolyatti) "Central Square (Tolyatti)").[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] The most famous central square is the monumentally-proportioned [Red Square](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Square "Red Square") which became a synecdoche for the [Soviet Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soviet_Union "Soviet Union") during the 20th century; nevertheless, the association with "red communism" is a back formation, since _krásnaja_ (the term for "red") also means "beautiful" in archaic and poetic Russian, with many cities and towns throughout the region having locations with the name "Red Square."[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

## Spanish-speaking countries and the Philippines

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Town_square&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Spanish-speaking countries and the Philippines")]

"Plaza mayor (urban design)" and "Plaza de Armas (urban design)" redirect here. For other uses, see [Plaza Mayor (disambiguation)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plaza_Mayor_(disambiguation) "Plaza Mayor (disambiguation)") and [Plaza de Armas (disambiguation)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plaza_de_Armas_(disambiguation) "Plaza de Armas (disambiguation)").

[![Image 17](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/44/Plaza_Mayor_de_Madrid_06.jpg/250px-Plaza_Mayor_de_Madrid_06.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Plaza_Mayor_de_Madrid_06.jpg)

[Plaza Mayor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plaza_Mayor,_Madrid "Plaza Mayor, Madrid"), Madrid, Spain

The [Spanish-language](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_language "Spanish language") term for a public square is _plaza_.[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piazza#cite_note-21) The term _plaza_ comes from [Latin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin "Latin")_platea_, with the meaning of 'broad street' or 'public square'.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piazza#cite_note-22) Ultimately coming from [Greek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ancient_Greek "Ancient Greek")πλατεῖα (ὁδός)_plateia (hodos)_, it is a cognate of Italian _piazza_ and French _place_ (which has also been borrowed into English).[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piazza#cite_note-etymology-23) The term is used across the [Spanish-speaking world](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hispanophone "Hispanophone"), including Spain, the Americas, and the [Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippines "Philippines").

In addition to smaller plazas, the _Plaza Mayor_ (sometimes called the _Plaza de Armas_[[b]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piazza#cite_note-24) in the Americas) of each administrative centre held three closely related institutions: the [cathedral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cathedral "Cathedral"), the _cantabile_ or administrative center, which might be incorporated in a wing of a governor's [palace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palace "Palace"), and the _audiencia_ or law court. The plaza might be large enough to serve as a military parade ground. Diminutives of _plaza_ include _plazuela_ and the latter's double diminutive _plazoleta_, which can be occasionally used as a particle in a proper noun.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piazza#cite_note-25)

In the former [Spanish Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_Empire "Spanish Empire"), most cities constructed by the Spanish _[conquistadores](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conquistador "Conquistador")_ were designed in a standard military fashion, based on a [grid pattern](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grid_pattern "Grid pattern")[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piazza#cite_note-26) taken from the [Roman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ancient_Rome "Ancient Rome")_[castrum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Castrum "Castrum")_, of which one block would be left vacant to form the Plaza de Armas. It is often surrounded by governmental buildings, churches, and other structures of cultural or political significance.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piazza#cite_note-27)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piazza#cite_note-28) The name derives from the fact that this would be a refuge in case of an attack upon the city, from which arms would be supplied to the defenders.

Like the Italian _piazza_ and the Portuguese _praça_, the plaza remains a center of community life that is only equaled by the market-place. A _plaza de toros_ is a [bullring](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bullring "Bullring"). [Shopping centers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shopping_center "Shopping center") may incorporate 'plaza' into their names, and _plaza comercial_ is used in some countries as a synonym for _centro comercial_ i.e. "shopping center".[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piazza#cite_note-29)

## United Kingdom

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Town_square&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: United Kingdom")]

In the [United Kingdom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Kingdom "United Kingdom"), and especially in [London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London "London") and [Edinburgh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edinburgh "Edinburgh"), a "square" has a wider meaning. There are public squares of the type described above, but the term is also used for formal open spaces surrounded by houses with private gardens at the centre, sometimes known as [garden squares](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garden_square "Garden square"). Most of these were built in the 18th and 19th centuries. In some cases the gardens are now open to the public. See the [Squares in London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Category:Squares_in_London "Category:Squares in London") category. Additionally, many public squares were created in towns and cities across the UK as part of urban redevelopment following [the Blitz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Blitz "The Blitz"). Squares can also be quite small and resemble courtyards, especially in the [City of London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_of_London "City of London").

## United States

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Town_square&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: United States")]

[![Image 18](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/30/Exterior_aerial_plaza_view%2C_facing_northwest._-_Los_Angeles_Music_Center%2C_135_North_Grand_Avenue%2C_Los_Angeles%2C_Los_Angeles_County%2C_CA_HABS_CA-2780-18.tif/lossy-page1-250px-Exterior_aerial_plaza_view%2C_facing_northwest._-_Los_Angeles_Music_Center%2C_135_North_Grand_Avenue%2C_Los_Angeles%2C_Los_Angeles_County%2C_CA_HABS_CA-2780-18.tif.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Exterior_aerial_plaza_view,_facing_northwest._-_Los_Angeles_Music_Center,_135_North_Grand_Avenue,_Los_Angeles,_Los_Angeles_County,_CA_HABS_CA-2780-18.tif)

[Los Angeles Music Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Music_Center "Los Angeles Music Center") Plaza

In some cities (in the [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States "United States")), especially in [New England](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_England "New England"), the term "square" (as its Spanish equivalent, _plaza_) is applied to a commercial area (like [Central Square](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Square_(Cambridge) "Central Square (Cambridge)") in [Cambridge, Massachusetts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cambridge,_Massachusetts "Cambridge, Massachusetts")), usually formed around the intersection of three or more streets, and which originally consisted of some open area (many of which have been filled in with traffic islands and other [traffic calming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Traffic_calming "Traffic calming") features). Many of these intersections are irregular rather than square.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piazza#cite_note-30)

The _placita_ (Spanish for "little plaza"), as it is known in the [Southwestern United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southwestern_United_States "Southwestern United States"), is a common feature within the boundaries of the former provincial kingdom of [Santa Fe de Nuevo México](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Fe_de_Nuevo_M%C3%A9xico "Santa Fe de Nuevo México"). They are a blend of [Hispano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Territorial_Style "Territorial Style") and [Pueblo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pueblo_architecture "Pueblo architecture") design styles, several of which continue to be hubs for cities and towns in [New Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico "New Mexico"), including [Santa Fe Plaza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Fe_Plaza "Santa Fe Plaza"), [Old Town Albuquerque](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Town_Albuquerque "Old Town Albuquerque"), [Acoma Pueblo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acoma_Pueblo "Acoma Pueblo")'s plaza, [Taos Downtown Historic District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taos_Downtown_Historic_District "Taos Downtown Historic District"), [Mesilla Plaza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mesilla_Plaza "Mesilla Plaza"), [Mora](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mora,_New_Mexico "Mora, New Mexico"), and [Las Vegas Plaza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Las_Vegas_Plaza_(Las_Vegas,_New_Mexico) "Las Vegas Plaza (Las Vegas, New Mexico)").

In [U.S. English](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._English "U.S. English"), a plaza can mean one of several things:[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piazza#cite_note-31)

*   a town square, as in the Spanish usage
*   "any open area usually located near urban buildings and often featuring walkways, trees and shrubs, places to sit, and sometimes shops"[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]
*   a [shopping center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shopping_center "Shopping center") of any size
*   a [toll plaza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toll_plaza "Toll plaza"), where traffic must temporarily stop to pay tolls
*   an area adjacent to an expressway that has service facilities (such as restaurants, gas stations, and restrooms)

Today's metropolitan landscapes often incorporate the plaza as a design element, or as an outcome of zoning regulations, building budgetary constraints, and the like. Sociologist [William H. Whyte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_H._Whyte "William H. Whyte") conducted an extensive study of plazas in [New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City "New York City"): his study humanized the way modern urban plazas are conceptualized, and helped usher in significant design changes in the making of plazas. They can be used to open spaces for low-income neighborhoods, and can also the overall aesthetic of the surrounding area boosting economic vitality, pedestrian mobility and safety for pedestrians.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piazza#cite_note-32) Most plazas are created out of a collaboration between local non-profit applicants and city officials which requires approval from the city.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piazza#cite_note-silverlake-33)

Throughout North America, words like _place_, _square_, or _plaza_ frequently appear in the names of commercial developments such as shopping centers and hotels.

[![Image 7](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/06/Saint_Peter%27s_Square_Argos.jpg/250px-Saint_Peter%27s_Square_Argos.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Saint_Peter's_Square_Argos.jpg)

The Saint Peter's Square is the heart of the Greek city of [Argos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Argos,_Peloponnese "Argos, Peloponnese").

A **town square** (or **public square**, **urban square**, **city square** or simply **square**), also called a **plaza** or **piazza**, is an open [public space](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_space "Public space") commonly found in the heart of a traditional [town](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Town "Town") or [city](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City "City"), and which may sometimes be used for community gatherings. Related concepts are the [civic center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Civic_center "Civic center"), the [market square](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Market_square "Market square") and the [village green](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Village_green "Village green").

Most squares are [hardscapes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hardscape "Hardscape") suitable for open [markets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Market_(place) "Market (place)"), [concerts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Concert "Concert"), political rallies, and other events that require firm ground. They are not necessarily a true [geometric square](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Square "Square").

Being centrally located, town squares are often surrounded by small shops such as bakeries, meat markets, cheese stores, and clothing stores. At their center is often a [well](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Well "Well"), [monument](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monument "Monument"), [statue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue "Statue") or other feature. Those with fountains are sometimes called fountain squares.

The term "town square" (especially via the term "public square") is synonymous with the politics of many cultures, and the names of a certain town squares, such as the [Euromaidan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euromaidan "Euromaidan") and [Red Square](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Square "Red Square"), have become symbolic of specific political events throughout history.

## Australia

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Town_square&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Australia")]

Many cities in Australia's eastern states, such as [Melbourne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Melbourne "Melbourne") and [Sydney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sydney "Sydney"), did not have a central town square in their design, due to a fear of rebellion. [New South Wales Governors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governor_of_New_South_Wales "Governor of New South Wales")[Richard Bourke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Bourke "Richard Bourke") and [George Gipps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Gipps "George Gipps") notably ordered surveyors to not include a town square in city designs, including Melbourne, to prevent the spirit of democracy from arising.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piazza#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piazza#cite_note-2)

The [city centre of Adelaide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adelaide_city_centre "Adelaide city centre") and the adjacent suburb of [North Adelaide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Adelaide "North Adelaide"), in [South Australia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Australia "South Australia"), were planned by [Colonel William Light](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colonel_William_Light "Colonel William Light") in 1837. The city streets were laid out in a [grid plan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grid_plan "Grid plan"), with the city centre including a central public square, [Victoria Square](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victoria_Square,_Adelaide "Victoria Square, Adelaide"), and four public squares in the centre of each quarter of the city. North Adelaide has two public squares. The city was also designed to be surrounded by [park lands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adelaide_park_lands "Adelaide park lands"), and all of these features still exist today, with the squares maintained as mostly green spaces.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piazza#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piazza#cite_note-4)

In 2025, the [City of Sydney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_of_Sydney "City of Sydney") council approved plans to accelerate the construction of a public square near the current [Town Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sydney_Town_Hall "Sydney Town Hall").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piazza#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piazza#cite_note-6)

In China, [People's Square](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People's_Square_(disambiguation) "People's Square (disambiguation)") is a common designation for the central town square of modern Chinese cities, established as part of urban modernization within the last few decades. These squares are the site of government buildings, museums, and other public buildings. One such square, [Tiananmen Square](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tiananmen_Square "Tiananmen Square"), is a famous site in Chinese history due to it being the site of the [May Fourth Movement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/May_Fourth_Movement "May Fourth Movement"), the [Proclamation of the People's Republic of China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proclamation_of_the_People's_Republic_of_China "Proclamation of the People's Republic of China"), the [1976 Tiananmen Incident](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1976_Tiananmen_Incident "1976 Tiananmen Incident"), the [1989 Tiananmen Square Protests](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1989_Tiananmen_Square_Protests "1989 Tiananmen Square Protests"), and all [Chinese National Day Parades](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_National_Day_Parade "Chinese National Day Parade").

## Italy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Town_square&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Italy")]

"Piazza" redirects here. For other uses, see [Piazza (disambiguation)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piazza_(disambiguation) "Piazza (disambiguation)").

[![Image 13](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/25/Piazza_Navona_1.jpg/250px-Piazza_Navona_1.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Piazza_Navona_1.jpg)

[Piazza Navona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piazza_Navona "Piazza Navona") and the [Fontana del Moro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fontana_del_Moro "Fontana del Moro") in [Rome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rome "Rome"), Italy. The fountain in the foreground is [Fontana dei Quattro Fiumi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fontana_dei_Quattro_Fiumi "Fontana dei Quattro Fiumi").

A _**piazza**_ (Italian pronunciation:[[ˈpjattsa]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Italian "Help:IPA/Italian")) is a [city square](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_square "City square") in [Italy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italy "Italy"), [Malta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malta "Malta"), along the [Dalmatian coast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalmatian_coast "Dalmatian coast") and in surrounding regions. Possibly influenced by the centrality of the [Roman forum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forum_(Roman) "Forum (Roman)") to ancient Mediterranean culture, the _piazze_ of Italy are central to most towns and cities. Shops, businesses, metro stations, and bus stops are commonly found on _piazzas_, and in multiple locations also feature [Roman Catholic churches](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roman_Catholic_churches "Roman Catholic churches"), such as in places known as the [Piazza del Duomo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piazza_del_Duomo_(disambiguation) "Piazza del Duomo (disambiguation)"), with the most famous perhaps being [the one in Milan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piazza_del_Duomo,_Milan "Piazza del Duomo, Milan"), or government buildings, such as the Piazza del Quirinale adjacent to the [Quirinal Palace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quirinal_Palace "Quirinal Palace") of the [Italian president](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_Italy "President of Italy") in Rome.

The [Piazza San Marco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piazza_San_Marco "Piazza San Marco") in [Venice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venice "Venice") and [Piazza del Popolo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piazza_del_Popolo "Piazza del Popolo") in Rome are among the world's best known Italian _piazzas_. These squares historically played a major role in the political developments of Italy in both the [Italian Medieval era](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italy_in_the_Middle_Ages "Italy in the Middle Ages") and the [Italian Renaissance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_Renaissance "Italian Renaissance").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piazza#cite_note-11) For example, the [Piazza della Signoria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piazza_della_Signoria "Piazza della Signoria") in [Florence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florence "Florence") remains synonymous with the return of the [Medici](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medici "Medici") from their exile in 1530 as well as the burning at the stake of [Savonarola](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Girolamo_Savonarola "Girolamo Savonarola").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piazza#cite_note-12)[Naples](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naples "Naples")' main square is [Piazza del Plebiscito](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piazza_del_Plebiscito "Piazza del Plebiscito").

The Italian term is roughly equivalent to the Spanish _[plaza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plaza "Plaza")_, French term _place_, Portuguese _praça_, and German _Platz_. The concept should not be confused with an unrelated usage of the term referring to a feature of architectural or urban design, such as the _piazza_ at [King's Cross station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London_King's_Cross_railway_station "London King's Cross railway station") in London or _piazza_ as a [verandah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Verandah "Verandah") or front [porch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Porch "Porch") of a house or apartment in the United States,[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piazza#cite_note-13) such as at [George Washington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Washington "George Washington")'s historic home [Mount Vernon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mount_Vernon "Mount Vernon").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piazza#cite_note-14)

Several countries, especially around the [Mediterranean Sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mediterranean_Sea "Mediterranean Sea"), feature Italian-style town squares. In Gibraltar, one such town square just off [Gibraltar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gibraltar "Gibraltar")'s [Main Street](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Main_Street,_Gibraltar "Main Street, Gibraltar"), between the [Parliament Building](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gibraltar_Parliament "Gibraltar Parliament") and the [City Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gibraltar_City_Hall "Gibraltar City Hall") officially named _[John Mackintosh Square](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John\_Mackintosh\_Square "John Mackintosh Square")_ is referred to as _The Piazza_.

## Netherlands and Belgium

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Town_square&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Netherlands and Belgium")]

[![Image 14](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f5/Grote_Markt_%289379072012%29.jpg/250px-Grote_Markt_%289379072012%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Grote_Markt_(9379072012).jpg)

[Grand-Place](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand-Place "Grand-Place") in [Brussels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels "Brussels"), Belgium

In the [Low Countries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Low_Countries "Low Countries"), squares are often called "markets" because of their usage as [marketplaces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marketplace "Marketplace"). Most towns and cities in Belgium and the southern part of the Netherlands have in their historical centre a _Grote Markt_ (literally "Big Market") in Dutch or _Grand-Place_ (literally "Grand Square") in French[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piazza#cite_note-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piazza#cite_note-16) (for example the [Grand-Place](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand-Place "Grand-Place") in [Brussels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels "Brussels") and the _[Grote Markt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grote\_Markt\_(Antwerp) "Grote Markt (Antwerp)")_ in [Antwerp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antwerp "Antwerp")). The _Grote Markt_ or _Grand-Place_ is often the location of the [town hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Town_hall "Town hall"), hence also the political centre of the town. The Dutch word for square is _plein_, which is another common name for squares in Dutch-speaking regions (for example [Het Plein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Het_Plein "Het Plein") in [The Hague](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Hague "The Hague")).

In the 17th and 18th centuries, another type of square emerged, the so-called _royal square_ (French: _Place royale_, Dutch: _Koningsplein_). Such squares did not serve as a marketplace but were built in front of large palaces or public buildings to emphasise their grandeur, as well as to accommodate [military parades](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_parade "Military parade") and ceremonies, among others (for example the [Place Royale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Place_Royale,_Brussels "Place Royale, Brussels") in Brussels and the [Koningsplein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koningsplein "Koningsplein") in [Amsterdam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amsterdam "Amsterdam")). Palace squares are usually more symmetrical than their older market counterparts.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piazza#cite_note-17)

## Spanish-speaking countries and the Philippines

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Town_square&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Spanish-speaking countries and the Philippines")]

"Plaza mayor (urban design)" and "Plaza de Armas (urban design)" redirect here. For other uses, see [Plaza Mayor (disambiguation)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plaza_Mayor_(disambiguation) "Plaza Mayor (disambiguation)") and [Plaza de Armas (disambiguation)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plaza_de_Armas_(disambiguation) "Plaza de Armas (disambiguation)").

[![Image 17](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/44/Plaza_Mayor_de_Madrid_06.jpg/250px-Plaza_Mayor_de_Madrid_06.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Plaza_Mayor_de_Madrid_06.jpg)

[Plaza Mayor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plaza_Mayor,_Madrid "Plaza Mayor, Madrid"), Madrid, Spain

The [Spanish-language](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_language "Spanish language") term for a public square is _plaza_.[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piazza#cite_note-21) The term _plaza_ comes from [Latin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin "Latin")_platea_, with the meaning of 'broad street' or 'public square'.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piazza#cite_note-22) Ultimately coming from [Greek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ancient_Greek "Ancient Greek")πλατεῖα (ὁδός)_plateia (hodos)_, it is a cognate of Italian _piazza_ and French _place_ (which has also been borrowed into English).[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piazza#cite_note-etymology-23) The term is used across the [Spanish-speaking world](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hispanophone "Hispanophone"), including Spain, the Americas, and the [Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippines "Philippines").

In addition to smaller plazas, the _Plaza Mayor_ (sometimes called the _Plaza de Armas_[[b]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piazza#cite_note-24) in the Americas) of each administrative centre held three closely related institutions: the [cathedral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cathedral "Cathedral"), the _cantabile_ or administrative center, which might be incorporated in a wing of a governor's [palace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palace "Palace"), and the _audiencia_ or law court. The plaza might be large enough to serve as a military parade ground. Diminutives of _plaza_ include _plazuela_ and the latter's double diminutive _plazoleta_, which can be occasionally used as a particle in a proper noun.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piazza#cite_note-25)

In the former [Spanish Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_Empire "Spanish Empire"), most cities constructed by the Spanish _[conquistadores](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conquistador "Conquistador")_ were designed in a standard military fashion, based on a [grid pattern](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grid_pattern "Grid pattern")[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piazza#cite_note-26) taken from the [Roman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ancient_Rome "Ancient Rome")_[castrum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Castrum "Castrum")_, of which one block would be left vacant to form the Plaza de Armas. It is often surrounded by governmental buildings, churches, and other structures of cultural or political significance.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piazza#cite_note-27)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piazza#cite_note-28) The name derives from the fact that this would be a refuge in case of an attack upon the city, from which arms would be supplied to the defenders.

Like the Italian _piazza_ and the Portuguese _praça_, the plaza remains a center of community life that is only equaled by the market-place. A _plaza de toros_ is a [bullring](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bullring "Bullring"). [Shopping centers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shopping_center "Shopping center") may incorporate 'plaza' into their names, and _plaza comercial_ is used in some countries as a synonym for _centro comercial_ i.e. "shopping center".[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piazza#cite_note-29)

## United Kingdom

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Town_square&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: United Kingdom")]

In the [United Kingdom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Kingdom "United Kingdom"), and especially in [London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London "London") and [Edinburgh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edinburgh "Edinburgh"), a "square" has a wider meaning. There are public squares of the type described above, but the term is also used for formal open spaces surrounded by houses with private gardens at the centre, sometimes known as [garden squares](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garden_square "Garden square"). Most of these were built in the 18th and 19th centuries. In some cases the gardens are now open to the public. See the [Squares in London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Category:Squares_in_London "Category:Squares in London") category. Additionally, many public squares were created in towns and cities across the UK as part of urban redevelopment following [the Blitz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Blitz "The Blitz"). Squares can also be quite small and resemble courtyards, especially in the [City of London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_of_London "City of London").

## United States

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Town_square&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: United States")]

[Los Angeles Music Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Music_Center "Los Angeles Music Center") Plaza

In some cities (in the [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States "United States")), especially in [New England](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_England "New England"), the term "square" (as its Spanish equivalent, _plaza_) is applied to a commercial area (like [Central Square](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Square_(Cambridge) "Central Square (Cambridge)") in [Cambridge, Massachusetts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cambridge,_Massachusetts "Cambridge, Massachusetts")), usually formed around the intersection of three or more streets, and which originally consisted of some open area (many of which have been filled in with traffic islands and other [traffic calming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Traffic_calming "Traffic calming") features). Many of these intersections are irregular rather than square.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piazza#cite_note-30)

The _placita_ (Spanish for "little plaza"), as it is known in the [Southwestern United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southwestern_United_States "Southwestern United States"), is a common feature within the boundaries of the former provincial kingdom of [Santa Fe de Nuevo México](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Fe_de_Nuevo_M%C3%A9xico "Santa Fe de Nuevo México"). They are a blend of [Hispano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Territorial_Style "Territorial Style") and [Pueblo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pueblo_architecture "Pueblo architecture") design styles, several of which continue to be hubs for cities and towns in [New Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico "New Mexico"), including [Santa Fe Plaza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Fe_Plaza "Santa Fe Plaza"), [Old Town Albuquerque](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Town_Albuquerque "Old Town Albuquerque"), [Acoma Pueblo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acoma_Pueblo "Acoma Pueblo")'s plaza, [Taos Downtown Historic District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taos_Downtown_Historic_District "Taos Downtown Historic District"), [Mesilla Plaza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mesilla_Plaza "Mesilla Plaza"), [Mora](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mora,_New_Mexico "Mora, New Mexico"), and [Las Vegas Plaza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Las_Vegas_Plaza_(Las_Vegas,_New_Mexico) "Las Vegas Plaza (Las Vegas, New Mexico)").

In [U.S. English](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._English "U.S. English"), a plaza can mean one of several things:[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piazza#cite_note-31)

*   a town square, as in the Spanish usage
*   "any open area usually located near urban buildings and often featuring walkways, trees and shrubs, places to sit, and sometimes shops"[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]
*   a [shopping center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shopping_center "Shopping center") of any size
*   a [toll plaza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toll_plaza "Toll plaza"), where traffic must temporarily stop to pay tolls
*   an area adjacent to an expressway that has service facilities (such as restaurants, gas stations, and restrooms)

Today's metropolitan landscapes often incorporate the plaza as a design element, or as an outcome of zoning regulations, building budgetary constraints, and the like. Sociologist [William H. Whyte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_H._Whyte "William H. Whyte") conducted an extensive study of plazas in [New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City "New York City"): his study humanized the way modern urban plazas are conceptualized, and helped usher in significant design changes in the making of plazas. They can be used to open spaces for low-income neighborhoods, and can also the overall aesthetic of the surrounding area boosting economic vitality, pedestrian mobility and safety for pedestrians.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piazza#cite_note-32) Most plazas are created out of a collaboration between local non-profit applicants and city officials which requires approval from the city.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piazza#cite_note-silverlake-33)

Throughout North America, words like _place_, _square_, or _plaza_ frequently appear in the names of commercial developments such as shopping centers and hotels.
